posts.title: GrapheneOS Apps I Use
posts.description: These are the apps I run on my Pixel with GrapheneOS . Each one has a short note on what it does, where to download it, and a URL you can paste into Obtainium to install it and keep it updated. Some links on this page are affiliate links (Proton Mail and Proton VPN). If you sign up through them I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. I only list apps and services I actually use. How to install apps with Obtainium Obtainium installs and updates apps straight from the developer's release page, so you get updates without needing a store account. Install Obtainium from GitHub Releases or F-Droid . Open Obtainium, tap Add App , and paste the Obtainium URL from the app you want below. Tap Add , then Install . Obtainium will ask for permission to install apps the first time. Every Obtainium URL below points to either the developer's own release page or F-Droid's official repository. posts.title: How to Block Ads with NextDNS
posts.description: In this guide, I show you how to blocks ads, trackers and scam websites at the DNS level across all of your devices for free using NextDNS. The service I recommend using is called NextDNS , which is a simple DNS management service which has community built block-lists which you can switch on to block ads, trackers, popups, phishing websites and more at the DNS level. On any device such as a phone or computer or Android TV, you simply set the DNS to the NextDNS server with the block-list, and all of those will be blocked automatically. NextDNS is free up to 300,000 DNS queries, which in the 5+ years of using it, I have not once gone over that for all of my device or come even close. An alternative to NextDNS would be hosting a Pi-Hole, which is basically a self-hosted version of NextDNS on your own WiFi network with an always on computer like a Raspberry Pi, then connecting to your WiFi always via TailScale or a similar solution to use that network. posts.title: How to Self-Host Navidrome on a VPS
posts.description: In this guide, I'm going to show you the simplest way to self-host your own Navidrome instance on a cheap VPS (virtual private server). This is a guide for complete beginners. If you want to self-host locally on your own hardware, I would recommend using this Beelink MINI S12 Pro Mini PC with an Intel N100 Processor and 16GB of RAM for self-hosting Navidrome. This guide will be the same instructions if you follow along on your own hardware running Debian 12 Linux Operating System. Navidrome is a free and open-source music management software that helps you stream or download your own personal music library from anywhere in the world. It basically becomes your own personal Spotify or Apple Music. Self-Hosted Navidrome Instance Sample With Navidrome, you must bring your own music files that Navidrome can read, and then it serves your music files through your self-hosted Navidrome instance.
